Substitute $y=vx$, so $dy = v\,dx + x\,dv$:
$x\sin v\,(v\,dx + x\,dv) = (vx\sin v - x)\,dx$, which gives $x^2\sin v\,dv = -x\,dx$
$\sin v\,dv = -\dfrac{dx}{x}$, so $-\cos v = -\ln x + C$
At $x=1$, $v=\pi/2$: $\cos(\pi/2)=0=\ln 1 + C'$, so $C'=0$. Hence $\cos\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) = \ln x$
$\alpha = \cos\left(\dfrac{y(e^{12})}{e^{12}}\right) = \ln e^{12} = 12$
Circle: $x^2+y^2-2px+2py+14=0$ has centre $(p,-p)$ and $r^2 = 2p^2 - 14$
For a real circle, $r^2>0$, so $p^2>7$. For $r\le 6$, $2p^2-14\le 36$, so $p^2\le 25$
The integers with $7<p^2\le 25$ are $p=\pm3,\pm4,\pm5$, which is 6 values
Answer: 6

Substitute $y=vx$, so $dy=v\,dx+x\,dv$:
$x\sin v\,(v\,dx+x\,dv)=(vx\sin v-x)\,dx$
Cancelling the $vx\sin v\,dx$ terms: $x^2\sin v\,dv=-x\,dx \Rightarrow \sin v\,dv=-\dfrac{dx}{x}$
Integrate: $-\cos v=-\ln x+C \Rightarrow \cos\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)=\ln x+C_1$
At $x=1$, $y=\frac{\pi}{2}$: $\cos\frac{\pi}{2}=0=\ln 1+C_1$, so $C_1=0$ and $\cos\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)=\ln x$
$\alpha=\cos\left(\dfrac{y(e^{12})}{e^{12}}\right)=\ln e^{12}=12$
The circle is $x^2+y^2-2px+2py+14=0$ with centre $(p,-p)$, so $r^2=p^2+p^2-14=2p^2-14$
For a real circle: $2p^2-14>0 \Rightarrow p^2>7$. The case $r=0$ needs $p^2=7$, which has no integer solution.
For $r\le 6$: $2p^2-14\le 36 \Rightarrow p^2\le 25$
So $7<p^2\le 25$, giving $p\in\{\pm3,\pm4,\pm5\}$: 6 values.
Answer: 6
